First release of DiskRescue: get photos and videos back from failing hard disks, SSDs, USB drives and SD cards, and repair the files that came back broken.

## Three ways to use it

- **`diskrescue-gui`**: desktop app. Pick the drive, press Rescue, browse your photos. Asks for administrator rights only when it needs them.
- **`diskrescue-tui`**: the same rescue flow inside a terminal (`sudo diskrescue-tui`).
- **`diskrescue`**: command line for scripts and experts (`list`, `info`, `image`, `scan`, `recover`, `carve`, `repair`, `verify`, `map`).

## What it does

- **Careful, resumable copies of failing drives**, with a strategy chosen from the device type (hard disk, SSD, USB pen drive, SD card). Survives USB drives that drop off the bus, re-checks data that some USB bridges return wrongly after errors, and keeps a GNU ddrescue compatible progress map.
- **Recovery by name** of existing and deleted files from FAT, exFAT, NTFS and ext4, including cards whose boot sector is destroyed ("needs formatting") and NTFS volumes with both boot sectors gone.
- **Carving** of more than 30 photo, RAW, video and audio formats from free or unreadable space, with exact file lengths.
- **Repair** of videos that will not open ("moov atom not found") using a healthy clip from the same camera or phone, of truncated or header-damaged JPEGs, broken PNGs and AVIs without an index.
- **Honest reports**: unreadable sectors are listed, never invented; partly recovered photos are marked as partial.

DiskRescue never writes to the drive it rescues and refuses to save output onto it.

## Downloads

`diskrescue_0.1.0_amd64.deb` installs all three programs with a menu entry on Ubuntu 24.04 and newer (`sudo apt install ./diskrescue_0.1.0_amd64.deb`). `diskrescue-v0.1.0-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` contains `diskrescue` and `diskrescue-tui` (static, run on any x86-64 Linux), `diskrescue-gui` (needs a desktop with X11 or Wayland), a `.desktop` entry, the icon, README and usage guide. Keep `diskrescue` next to `diskrescue-gui`: the desktop app uses it to copy drives with administrator rights.

## Known limits

- Tested on synthetic disk images, simulated failing devices and generated media; not yet on a wide range of real failing hardware or real camera RAW files.
- Windows builds compile but have not been run on Windows; no Windows binaries in this release.
- Deleted files on SSDs are usually erased by TRIM and rarely recoverable.
- Not yet supported: fragmented-file carving, APFS, HFS+, btrfs, XFS, encrypted volumes.
